headline: `b.auth.sdJwtVc.verify` refuses a credential whose `nbf` (not-before) is in the future
summary: `b.auth.sdJwtVc.verify` validated a credential's `exp` (expiry) but did not check `nbf` (not-before), so an issuer-signed SD-JWT verifiable credential presented before its activation time verified as valid. It now refuses such a credential with `auth-sd-jwt-vc/not-yet-valid`, matching the not-before check the other token verifiers already apply.

items.title: sdJwtVc.verify enforces the not-before (nbf) claim
items.body: `b.auth.sdJwtVc.verify` checked `iat` (not in the future) and `exp` (not expired) but had no `nbf` (not-before) check, so an issuer-signed credential carrying a future `nbf` verified as valid before its activation time, including when reached through `b.auth.oid4vp` presentation verification. A credential whose `nbf` is more than the clock-skew tolerance in the future is now refused with `auth-sd-jwt-vc/not-yet-valid`, matching the not-before enforcement already in the JWT, external-JWT, and OIDC ID-token verifiers. A credential with no `nbf`, or one within the skew window, is unaffected.
